chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu‘allā ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Abd Allah, from Ibn Mas‘ūd, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Ibrahim al-Ja‘farī, who said:

I heard Isḥāq ibn Ja‘far saying: I heard my father saying: The awṣiyāʾ, when their mothers conceive them, she is overcome by a period resembling a fainting spell. She remains in that state for that day if it is daytime, or for that night if it is nighttime. Then she sees in her sleep a man giving her glad tidings of a knowledgeable, forbearing boy, and she rejoices because of that.

She awakens from her sleep and hears from her right side, at the side of the house, a voice saying: You have conceived with خير, you will proceed to خير, and you have come with خير. Receive glad tidings of a forbearing, knowledgeable boy. She then feels lightness in her body, and after that she no longer finds heaviness in her sides and belly. When she reaches the ninth month, she hears an intense sound in the house. Then on the night in which she gives birth, a light appears to her in the house that she sees, and none sees it besides her except his father.

Then when she gives birth to him, she gives birth to him seated, and she opens for him until he emerges cross-legged. After falling to the ground, he turns so that his face does not miss the qiblah wherever it may be. Then he sneezes three times, gesturing with his finger in praise, and he falls with the umbilical cord cut and circumcised, with his four incisors above and below, his canines, and his molars. Between his hands there is a light like a bar of gold, and throughout his day and night his hands flow with gold. Thus also are the Prophets when they are born, and the awṣiyāʾ are but offshoots from the Prophets.

key_terms.أَعْلَاقٌ: attachments or offshoots, indicating the awṣiyāʾ as derived from the Prophets
key_terms.سَبِيكَةِ ٱلذَّهَبِ: a bar or ingot of gold, used to describe the luminous radiance before him
key_terms.غُلَامٍ عَلِيمٍ حَلِيمٍ: a boy described as knowledgeable and forbearing
key_terms.فَتْرَةٌ: a temporary state or interval, here resembling a fainting condition during conception
key_terms.مَسْرُورًا مَخْتُونًا: born with the umbilical cord cut and already circumcised
key_terms.ٱلْأَنْبِيَاءُ: the Prophets, whose births are said to share similar signs
key_terms.ٱلْأَوْصِيَاءُ: the designated successors, referring to the divinely appointed heirs after the Prophets
key_terms.ٱلْقِبْلَةَ: the direction of prayer, toward which the newborn turns his face

ai.seo_question: What signs are mentioned in hadith about the conception and birth of the awṣiyāʾ and Imams?
ai.summary: This hadith describes extraordinary signs associated with the conception and birth of the awṣiyāʾ, portraying them as divinely marked from the womb through birth. It also links these signs to the Prophets, presenting the awṣiyāʾ as a continuation from them and emphasizing their sacred status in Shia theology.
